title: Rings of Numbers With Prime Sums

concept.title: Fix the first number to avoid counting rotations
body: Arrange the numbers `1 .. n` in a circle so that every two neighbours (including the last and the first) add up to a **prime number**. Count the arrangements. A circle can be turned, so to avoid counting the same ring `n` times we **fix** the number 1 in the first place: all rings are written starting from 1, going around in one direction. (The same ring read in the opposite direction is a different arrangement here and counts separately.)

body.code:
def count(ring, used):
    if len(ring) == n:
        return 1 if prime[ring[-1] + ring[0]] else 0     # close the circle
    total = 0
    for v in range(2, n + 1):
        if not used[v] and prime[ring[-1] + v]:         # the new neighbour sum must be prime
            used[v] = True
            ring.append(v)
            total += count(ring, used)
            ring.pop()
            used[v] = False
    return total

body: The sum of two numbers is at most `2n`, so a table of primes up to `2n` answers every question at once (a **sieve**). Two odd numbers add up to an even number above 2, which is never prime, so in any ring odd and even numbers must alternate: for an odd `n` there are no rings. The search finds this out by itself, but only after trying many starts, so the limit is `n <= 14`.

statement: Count the ways to write the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` in a circle, starting with 1 and going around in one direction, so that every two neighbouring numbers add up to a prime number (the last number and the first number are also neighbours). The same circle read in the opposite direction is counted as a different way.
hints: Fix 1 as the first number of the ring.
A new number can follow the last one only if their sum is prime.
When all numbers are placed, check that the last number and 1 also add up to a prime.

explanation: The ring starts with 1; each next number must be unused and sum to a prime with the previous one. When all `n` numbers are placed, the closing sum with the first number must be prime too.
solution.complexity: Time about 60 000 steps for n = 14, space O(n).

code.python:
def count(n, ring, used, prime):
    if len(ring) == n:
        return 1 if prime[ring[-1] + ring[0]] else 0
    total = 0
    for v in range(2, n + 1):
        if not used[v] and prime[ring[-1] + v]:
            used[v] = True
            ring.append(v)
            total += count(n, ring, used, prime)
            ring.pop()
            used[v] = False
    return total

n = int(input())

prime = [x >= 2 and all(x % d != 0 for d in range(2, int(x ** 0.5) + 1)) for x in range(2 * n + 1)]
print(count(n, [1], [False] * (n + 1), prime))
